Recorded as a SEPARATE row from the 'Thrombocytopenia' row above because ClinicalTrials.gov posts them as two distinct MedDRA terms in two different system organ classes — 'Platelet Count Decreased' under Investigations (a laboratory finding) versus 'Thrombocytopenia' under Blood and lymphatic system disorders (a clinical diagnosis). rows.source_table: ClinicalTrials.gov Results > Adverse Events > 'Other (Not Including Serious) Adverse Events', term 'Thrombocytopenia', Blood and lymphatic system disorders: 25 of 81 subjects, group EG000 (OGX-011 Intent to Treat Analysis Set)
rows.notes: 25/81 = 30.9%. Non-serious treatment-emergent AE table, posted frequency threshold 5%. CONFOUNDING — READ BEFORE MODELLING: single-arm phase 1/2 study of custirsen PLUS gemcitabine 1250 mg/m2 (days 1,8) PLUS cisplatin 75 mg/m2 or carboplatin AUC5 (day 1). Gemcitabine and carboplatin are both strongly thrombocytopenic in their own right and there is NO comparator arm, so this incidence cannot be attributed to custirsen; effect_vs_control is TBD for that reason. GRADE 2 rationale: a named clinical thrombocytopenia AE in ~1 in 3 patients, classified non-serious (which excludes the grade-3 band, since serious platelet events are captured separately in the two rows below). ClinicalTrials.gov non-serious AE tables carry no CTCAE grade, so the severity band is unstated and grade 2 is the mid-band assignment, not a read value.

rows.source_table: ClinicalTrials.gov Results > Adverse Events > 'Serious Adverse Events', term 'Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura', Blood and lymphatic system disorders: 1 of 81 subjects, group EG000
rows.notes: 1/81 = 1.2%. THE MOST SEVERE PLATELET EVENT RECORDED FOR CUSTIRSEN in any source I could fetch. Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is a thrombotic microangiopathy defined by consumptive thrombocytopenia, hence is_platelet_specific=TRUE and readout_category=clinical_outcome (a clinical syndrome rather than a platelet count measurement). GRADE 3 by the rubric's severe band (serious, life-threatening platelet-consumptive event). ATTRIBUTION CAUTION: gemcitabine is itself a recognised cause of drug-induced thrombotic microangiopathy, this is a single-arm study, and ClinicalTrials.gov posts no causality assessment for this term — so this event cannot be attributed to custirsen. It is recorded as an observed severe platelet event under custirsen exposure, not as custirsen-caused.

rows.source_table: ClinicalTrials.gov Results > Adverse Events > 'Serious Adverse Events' (complete 23-term table), group EG001 'OGX-011 / Docetaxel/Prednisone', n=46 at risk — no thrombocytopenia or platelet term present
rows.notes: EXPLICIT ZERO, per the schema's rule that a tabulated severe band with no events is a grade-0 row rather than a missing row. HAD EVENTS OCCURRED THIS CELL WOULD HAVE CARRIED GRADE 3. Justification that this is a real zero and not merely silence: the ClinicalTrials.gov Serious Adverse Events table is a complete tabulation reported at any frequency, and it IS populated for this arm (23 distinct terms including Febrile Neutropenia, Gastrointestinal Haemorrhage, Haematuria and Death), so the absence of any thrombocytopenia or platelet term means zero serious platelet events in 46 patients. Additionally, no thrombocytopenia or platelet term appears in the non-serious AE table either, which is posted at a 5% frequency threshold — so non-serious thrombocytopenia also occurred in <5% of this arm (the blood/investigations terms that did clear 5% were Anaemia 8/46, Neutropenia 4/46, Weight Decreased 8/46, AST Increased 0/46). NO COMPARATOR: both arms of this trial received custirsen, so effect_vs_control is TBD.

rows.source_ref: PMID 23836992 / PMC3699352 / doi:10.2147/OTT.S33077 (Higano CS. OncoTargets Ther. 2013;6:785-797)
rows.source_table: Section 'Tolerability of custirsen', paragraph 1 — reporting ref 65 = Chi KN et al., J Natl Cancer Inst 2005;97:1287-96 (PMID 16145049; NCT00054106)
rows.notes: HIGHEST-ATTRIBUTION HUMAN ROW IN THIS SET. Verbatim: "In the first Phase I study of custirsen in prostate cancer, no dose-limiting toxicities were reported at the doses of custirsen investigated (up to 640 mg); all toxicities were grade 1/2 and typically occurred within the first week of administration. For patients receiving the 640 mg dose, the most frequent adverse events included thrombocytopenia, anemia, and leukopenia". GRADE 1 rationale: the source explicitly caps ALL toxicities at CTCAE grade 1/2 and reports no DLTs and no intervention, which is the rubric's mild/reversible band. readout_value=TBD because the source names thrombocytopenia as a most-frequent AE but prints no incidence figure — not estimated. WHY THIS ROW MATTERS: NCT00054106 (verified on ClinicalTrials.gov) is 'A Phase I Study Of Combination Neoadjuvant Hormone Therapy And Weekly OGX-011 Prior To Radical Prostatectomy', interventions buserelin + flutamide + custirsen sodium + surgery. There is NO cytotoxic chemotherapy, so unlike every other custirsen clinical row below, this thrombocytopenia signal is not confounded by a myelosuppressive backbone. Corroborated by the primary paper's own abstract (PMID 16145049): "Only grade 1 and 2 toxicities were observed" across 40-640 mg in n=25. I could not obtain the JNCI full text (Unpaywall oa_status=closed) so the per-dose toxicity table was not read.

rows.exposure_duration: single 640 mg dose (Group A) or escalating 320/480/640 mg over 6 days then 640 mg on day 8 (Group B); 120-min IV infusion
rows.source_ref: PMID 25782535 / PMC4574829 / doi:10.1111/bcp.12633 (Rabinovich-Guilatt L et al., Br J Clin Pharmacol 2015;80:436-45)
rows.source_table: Abstract (Results) — "AEs included CS, elevated transaminases and prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) that were predominantly grade 1/2"; corroborated against the full-text adverse-event table (Table 1) read via PMC
rows.notes: ADJACENT-HAEMATOLOGY FALLBACK ROW — is_platelet_specific=FALSE. Included because it is the ONLY custirsen exposure in humans I could find that is free of a cytotoxic chemotherapy backbone AND free of cancer: 22 healthy subjects (Group A n=10, Group B n=12) at the full 640 mg clinical dose with dexamethasone premedication. aPTT prolongation is the classic PS-ASO class coagulation effect and is the nearest measured haemostasis endpoint. Verbatim second finding: "Increasing doses of custirsen may have mitigated the severity but not incidence of aPTT prolongation". readout_value=TBD: the abstract gives no aPTT number and I could not retrieve the numeric results table (the publisher blocks XML full-text download; only the rendered PMC page was readable). GRADE 0 CAVEAT — READ THIS: the grade refers to the platelet endpoint, and platelets are NEVER mentioned anywhere in this paper. I am treating it as a weak explicit zero rather than mere silence because the paper DOES tabulate treatment-emergent laboratory AEs and reports a haematology one ('Lymphocyte count decreased', 1 subject (10%), Group A, grade 2) alongside transaminase and aPTT abnormalities, while no platelet AE appears — i.e. routine haematology was assessed and no platelet event met the reporting threshold. I did NOT create a separate is_platelet_specific=TRUE grade-0 platelet row from this paper, because that would be exactly the forbidden 'source did not mention platelets, therefore grade 0' inference.

rows.exposure_duration: chronic (weekly with taxane chemotherapy, pooled across 3 RCTs)
rows.effect_vs_control: OR 2.62 (95% CI 1.82-3.77), P<.001 vs chemotherapy alone
rows.source_table: Results section 3.3 'Efficacy and safety' (text) and Fig 3D (forest plot, thrombocytopenia)
rows.notes: THE ONLY CONTROLLED CUSTIRSEN PLATELET ESTIMATE I could obtain, and the strongest causal-attribution row here. Meta-analysis of 3 randomized controlled trials, 1709 patients (857 custirsen + docetaxel-or-cabazitaxel + prednisone vs 852 chemotherapy + prednisone alone). Because both arms receive the same myelosuppressive taxane backbone, the odds ratio isolates the custirsen increment: adding custirsen multiplies the odds of thrombocytopenia 2.62-fold. Verbatim: "thrombocytopenia (OR = 2.62, 95% CI = 1.82-3.77, P < .001)". GRADE 2 rationale: a named thrombocytopenia adverse event, significantly more frequent on custirsen and reported by the authors as a treatment-related complication requiring clinical attention, places it above the mild band; the source prints NO CTCAE severity band and no platelet counts, so grade 3 is not supportable and was not assigned. This is a grading judgement on an unstated severity, flagged accordingly. Licence is CC-BY-NC-ND (read from the article's own licence field), i.e. NOT CC-BY, hence summary_stat rather than cc_by.

rows.exposure_duration: days 1, 3, 5 of cycle 1 then weekly IV until progression, with acalabrutinib 100 mg PO bid
rows.source_table: Results, 'Primary endpoint: safety' ('AEs that led to discontinuation of danvatirsen were ALT increased, lower gastrointestinal hemorrhage, edema, and platelet count decreased, each occurring in 1 patient')
rows.notes: Graded 3 directly on the rubric's 'treatment discontinuation for a platelet event' criterion - this is the clearest clinically-actionable danvatirsen platelet outcome in the dataset. The same sentence records that platelet count decreased ALSO led to discontinuation of acalabrutinib in 1 patient, presumably the same individual (both drugs stopped); recorded here once, against danvatirsen, rather than twice. Likely the same patient as one of the 4 grade >=3 platelet-count-decreased cases, so do not aggregate.

rows.exposure_duration: days 1, 3, 5 of cycle 1 then weekly IV until progression, with acalabrutinib 100 mg PO bid
rows.source_table: Table 2 'Most common AEs occurring in >=10% of patients, regardless of relationship to study treatment', row 'Platelet count decreased', Any grade column
rows.notes: PRISM module 1 (NCT03527147), acalabrutinib + danvatirsen in relapsed/refractory DLBCL, n=17. Platelet count decreased was joint-second most common AE overall (47%), behind anaemia (53%). Graded 1 for the ANY-GRADE composite; 4 of these 8 were grade >=3 and are carried in a separate row, so do not sum the two rows. MAJOR CONFOUND, stated: acalabrutinib is a BTK inhibitor with its own platelet/bleeding liability and there is no danvatirsen-monotherapy arm here, so this row cannot attribute the effect to the ASO alone - the cohort-1 monotherapy rows from PMC9594513 are the compound-attributable comparator. Note also that Table 2 reports 'Platelet count decreased' and 'Thrombocytopenia' as SEPARATE MedDRA preferred terms, so the true patient-level burden lies between 47% and 65% depending on overlap, which the paper does not resolve.

rows.exposure_duration: days 1, 3, 5 of cycle 1 then weekly IV until progression, with acalabrutinib 100 mg PO bid
rows.notes: Graded 1 on ATTRIBUTION, not on the keyword. The source does not attribute any epistaxis to thrombocytopenia, and acalabrutinib - a BTK inhibitor - independently causes bleeding through impaired platelet FUNCTION at normal platelet counts. Grading this 3 because one event was grade >=3 and the cohort also had thrombocytopenia would manufacture an attributed haemorrhage out of an unattributed one. is_platelet_specific FALSE. A separate lower gastrointestinal haemorrhage led to discontinuation of both drugs in 1 patient (Results, 'Primary endpoint: safety'); it is likewise unattributed to platelet count and is recorded here in notes rather than as a grade-3 row.

rows.exposure_duration: days 1, 3, 5 of cycle 1 then weekly IV until progression, with acalabrutinib 100 mg PO bid
rows.source_table: Table 2, row 'Platelet count decreased', Grade >=3 column
rows.notes: 4/17 (24%) reached CTCAE grade >=3 (<50 x10^9/L), hence schema grade 3. Same acalabrutinib confound and same overlap caveat with the 'Thrombocytopenia' preferred term as the any-grade row. Extraction note on the source XML: the percentages in the Grade >=3 column are wrapped in bibliographic cross-reference tags by the PMC converter (e.g. '4 (<xref rid=bib24>24</xref>)'); they were verified as PERCENTAGES, not citations, by checking against n=17 (4/17=23.5%~24, 8/17=47%, 3/17=17.6%~18, 2/17=11.8%~12). A naive text scrape of this table will mis-read them.

rows.exposure_duration: days 1, 3, 5 of cycle 1 then weekly IV until progression, with acalabrutinib 100 mg PO bid
rows.notes: 2/17 (12%) grade >=3 thrombocytopenia (<50 x10^9/L), schema grade 3. Distinct preferred term from 'Platelet count decreased'; overlap unresolved by the source, so do not sum with the 24% grade >=3 platelet-count-decreased row. Acalabrutinib confound applies. The study protocol pre-specified platelet count decrease as a dose-limiting toxicity only when grade 3 WITH grade >=3 bleeding, or grade 4.
